notes: scan_record_url was null; digicoll search found record 264232 (Josefa de Haro, Claimant, Case no. 381 ND, 'Potrero de San Francisco (also called Potrero Nuevo)'). Count leaf (image 2): 'LAND CASE 381 ND 400 pgs.' Board opinion (Farwell, stamped PAGES 189-194) held the purported 24 May 1844 ratification of the 1 May provisional grant 'beyond a doubt... a forgery' but confirmed on the later-produced 18 Sept 1844 grant; the District Court and Supreme Court reversed that and rejected the claim outright. Ramon and Francisco de Haro Jr. (twin sons of Francisco de Haro Sr.) were both killed in 1846 (opinion PAGE 189: 'both killed during the war with America in the year 1846'); their father inherited, died ~1849/1850, leaving the petitioners as heirs. Register's year/governor/grantee describe the purported 1844 Micheltorena concession accurately, but no valid grant was ever finally recognized.

name.evidence: Red label (image 1): 'CASE No. 422 NORTHERN DISTRICT — LANDS OF THE CHRISTIAN INDIANS GRANT — JOSEPH S. ALEMANY CLAIMANT'; certification stamped PAGE 63: 'for the place known by the name of Lands of the Christianized Indians'. The register's composite description matches the petition's four claims exactly (stamped PAGES 11-14): one square league at each of the 21 missions; Las Gallinas, el Nacimiento and La Estrella; vacant lands of Santa Clara; tracts to named Santa Ines Indians.

year.evidence: All the instruments are of 1844: Santa Ines order 'bears date January 18, 1844' (stamped PAGE 13); Santa Clara grant 'dated June 10th 1844' (PAGE 12; opinion PAGE 58: 'made June 10, 1844 of all the vacant lands of Santa Clara ungranted before that time'); Gallinas/Nacimiento/Estrella grant 'dated July 16, 1844' (PAGE 12; opinion PAGE 55: 'The grant made by Governor Micheltorena and dated July 16, 1844 is presented and the signatures proved'); San Luis Obispo pueblo decree 'dated July 15, 1844' (PAGE 14).

governor.evidence: Every instrument is Micheltorena's: petition PAGE 12 'From Governor Manuel Micheltorena a grant of the lands known by the names of Las Gallinas, el Nacimiento and La Estrella...'; PAGE 14 'A decree of Manuel Micheltorena Governor of California dated July 15, 1844'; opinion PAGE 60: 'a decree in accordance with the Priest's recommendation signed by Governor Micheltorena'.

grantee.evidence: Register holds the grantees, not the claimant: grants ran 'To your petitioners the Christian Indians of San Miguel' (stamped PAGE 12), 'to your petitioners the Christian Indians of Santa Clara' (PAGE 12), to sixteen named Santa Ines neophytes (PAGES 12-13), and 'granting the Common lands to the Emancipated Indians' of San Luis Obispo (PAGE 14). Bishop Alemany filed 'on their behalf and as their guardian and trustee' (PAGE 12).

land_case.evidence: The Bancroft docket is ND 422 alone: red label 'CASE No. 422 NORTHERN DISTRICT'; D.C. caption stamped PAGE 64: 'D.C. 422: L.C. 663'. The register's 'ND/SD 422' hedge has a real basis but is imprecise: the Board ordered three transcripts because 'the land hereby adjudicated is situated both in the Northern and Southern Districts of California', one for the District Court of each district (decree stamped PAGE 62) — but the case as docketed and dismissed is Northern District No. 422 (Land Commission No. 663).

outcome.evidence: Board opinion by Com. Felch, stamped PAGE 61: 'We are of opinion that the proof will not warrant a Confirmation, and an adverse decree will be entered. Rejected.' Decree stamped PAGE 62: 'the claim of the said petitioner is not valid, and it is therefore decreed that the application for a Confirmation thereof be denied' (Felch, Thompson, Farwell, filed 31 Dec 1855). District Court, 23 Feb 1857, Hoffman J., stamped PAGE 64: no notice of appeal filed within the time limited by law, 'Ordered that this case be dismissed and struck from the docket of this Court' — rejection final. Register 'Rejected' matches.
